look_here_first: Start with bark, racemes, and leaf glands. Black cherry has alternate finely serrate leaves, elongated racemes of white flowers followed by black drupes, and older bark breaking into dark scaly plates. Local Edwards Plateau plants are commonly the accepted var. eximia.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small petiole glands near blade base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: local Edwards Plateau form commonly var. eximia

lookalikes.differences: P. mexicana flowers earlier in showier short clusters before leaf-out and has plum-like fruits. P. caroliniana is evergreen with glossy leaves and short axillary racemes. P. rivularis is a smaller thicket-forming plum.
